parts:
Hi Ben,

Thanks for the message.  Let me start by pointing you here to see if you've updated nimble and covered your bases on R 4.0 issues: https://r-nimble.org/download  There were some changes in R 4.0 that necessitated nimble 0.9.1 and attention to Rtools installation changes.

Please send another message if you can't resolve it from the information there.

-Perry
On Fri, Jun 26, 2020 at 12:31 PM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:

Hello,

I'm revisiting a NIMBLE sampler I wrote a few months ago, which worked fine at the time. I am now getting the error below saying it failed to create the shared library. I'm not sure if this is a Windows/R4.0 issue, but I followed all the instructions for installing Rtools 4.0 and it works to build packages/etc. Any ideas?

Thanks.

Ben

Thanks for the message.  Let me start by pointing you here to see if you've updated nimble and covered your bases on R 4.0 issues: https://r-nimble.org/download  There were some changes in R 4.0 that necessitated nimble 0.9.1 and attention to Rtools installation changes.

-Perry

messages.subject: Re: failed to create shared library in R 4.0
parts:
Apologies, this turned out to be user error. I forgot that I needed to change the dimensions of an object in a custom function in a specific situation. My past self put the comment about this issue in a suboptimal place. Thanks!

Ben

On Tuesday, June 30, 2020 at 10:43:17 AM UTC-4 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:
That suggests your compiler/system tools are fine. 

If you can share a reproducible example (on or off list) that would be helpful. Also given you said the model used to work if you could tell us what version of nimble your reproducible example works on, that would be helpful.

-chris

On Fri, Jun 26, 2020 at 1:43 PM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:
Also, I tried a different nimble model and it compiles. Not sure if that is helpful information or not.

On Friday, June 26, 2020 at 4:38:43 PM UTC-4 baug...@vt.edu wrote:
Yes, the path variables appear to be fine and I'm using nimble 0.9.1. I've looked at the other messages on the listserv about switching to R 4.0 and they haven't solved my problem so far.

In my path are:
C:\rtools40\
C:\rtools40\mingw_64\bin

On Friday, June 26, 2020 at 3:53:56 PM UTC-4 pdevalpine wrote:
Hi Ben,

Thanks for the message.  Let me start by pointing you here to see if you've updated nimble and covered your bases on R 4.0 issues: https://r-nimble.org/download  There were some changes in R 4.0 that necessitated nimble 0.9.1 and attention to Rtools installation changes.

Please send another message if you can't resolve it from the information there.

-Perry




On Fri, Jun 26, 2020 at 12:31 PM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:
Hello,

I'm revisiting a NIMBLE sampler I wrote a few months ago, which worked fine at the time. I am now getting the error below saying it failed to create the shared library. I'm not sure if this is a Windows/R4.0 issue, but I followed all the instructions for installing Rtools 4.0 and it works to build packages/etc. Any ideas?

Thanks.

Ben

Apologies, this turned out to be user error. I forgot that I needed to change the dimensions of an object in a custom function in a specific situation. My past self put the comment about this issue in a suboptimal place. Thanks!

Ben

On Tuesday, June 30, 2020 at 10:43:17 AM UTC-4 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:
That suggests your compiler/system tools are fine. 

If you can share a reproducible example (on or off list) that would be helpful. Also given you said the model used to work if you could tell us what version of nimble your reproducible example works on, that would be helpful.

-chris

Thanks for the message.  Let me start by pointing you here to see if you've updated nimble and covered your bases on R 4.0 issues: https://r-nimble.org/download  There were some changes in R 4.0 that necessitated nimble 0.9.1 and attention to Rtools installation changes.

Please send another message if you can't resolve it from the information there.

-Perry

messages.subject: Re: failed to create shared library in R 4.0
parts:
@Ben and others -- I am curious whether the custom function was actually the root cause? I suggest this only because I am getting this error when attempting to  `compileModel` on one machine on which I am working and have yet to resolve Rtools issues -- but the same code and data compiles fine on two other machines. 

Suggesting this here in case other folks find Ben's OP and are diverted from addressing Rtools issues further.

On Wednesday, July 1, 2020 at 12:50:56 PM UTC-6 pdevalpine wrote:
No problem - thanks for the update.


On Wed, Jul 1, 2020 at 11:19 AM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:
Apologies, this turned out to be user error. I forgot that I needed to change the dimensions of an object in a custom function in a specific situation. My past self put the comment about this issue in a suboptimal place. Thanks!

Ben

On Tuesday, June 30, 2020 at 10:43:17 AM UTC-4 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:
That suggests your compiler/system tools are fine. 

If you can share a reproducible example (on or off list) that would be helpful. Also given you said the model used to work if you could tell us what version of nimble your reproducible example works on, that would be helpful.

-chris

On Fri, Jun 26, 2020 at 1:43 PM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:
Also, I tried a different nimble model and it compiles. Not sure if that is helpful information or not.

On Friday, June 26, 2020 at 4:38:43 PM UTC-4 baug...@vt.edu wrote:
Yes, the path variables appear to be fine and I'm using nimble 0.9.1. I've looked at the other messages on the listserv about switching to R 4.0 and they haven't solved my problem so far.

In my path are:
C:\rtools40\
C:\rtools40\mingw_64\bin

On Friday, June 26, 2020 at 3:53:56 PM UTC-4 pdevalpine wrote:
Hi Ben,

Thanks for the message.  Let me start by pointing you here to see if you've updated nimble and covered your bases on R 4.0 issues: https://r-nimble.org/download  There were some changes in R 4.0 that necessitated nimble 0.9.1 and attention to Rtools installation changes.

Please send another message if you can't resolve it from the information there.

-Perry




On Fri, Jun 26, 2020 at 12:31 PM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:
Hello,

I'm revisiting a NIMBLE sampler I wrote a few months ago, which worked fine at the time. I am now getting the error below saying it failed to create the shared library. I'm not sure if this is a Windows/R4.0 issue, but I followed all the instructions for installing Rtools 4.0 and it works to build packages/etc. Any ideas?

Thanks.

Ben

messages.author: d4880d80370a2c2a
messages.subject: Re: failed to create shared library in R 4.0
parts:
Oops -- forgot to include note on why I suspect it was, in fact, an Rtools issue:
When attempting to run:
>     Rmodel.comp <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
I receive error:
> Error: Failed to create the shared library. Run 'printErrors()' to see the compilation errors.

Running:
> printErrors() 
yields:
> In system(cmd) : 'make' not found

Which suggests and Rtools issue (unless the error is misleading, which I suspect it isn't).

On Sunday, May 15, 2022 at 8:27:37 AM UTC-6 Jessica Burnett wrote:
@Ben and others -- I am curious whether the custom function was actually the root cause? I suggest this only because I am getting this error when attempting to  `compileModel` on one machine on which I am working and have yet to resolve Rtools issues -- but the same code and data compiles fine on two other machines. 

Suggesting this here in case other folks find Ben's OP and are diverted from addressing Rtools issues further.


On Wednesday, July 1, 2020 at 12:50:56 PM UTC-6 pdevalpine wrote:
No problem - thanks for the update.


On Wed, Jul 1, 2020 at 11:19 AM baug...@vt.edu <baug...@vt.edu> wrote:
Apologies, this turned out to be user error. I forgot that I needed to change the dimensions of an object in a custom function in a specific situation. My past self put the comment about this issue in a suboptimal place. Thanks!

Ben

On Tuesday, June 30, 2020 at 10:43:17 AM UTC-4 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:
That suggests your compiler/system tools are fine. 

If you can share a reproducible example (on or off list) that would be helpful. Also given you said the model used to work if you could tell us what version of nimble your reproducible example works on, that would be helpful.
